known_limitations: All models are synthetic / analytic toys calibrated to textbook zebra-finch HVC values (order stereotypy > 99%, syllable-duration CV ~ 5-15%, sub-ms spike-timing precision over a ~1 s song); NO neural data are touched, so the decisive observable is a proxy, not paper-faithful. The lambda-budget V(T)=D*(exp(2*lambda*T)-1)/(2*lambda) is a 1-D linear-noise model of timing dispersion, not a full E-I threshold-linear network simulation. The saddle-exit variance identity Var(tau)=Var(ln|z|)/lambda^2 holds for the 1-D normal-form exit tau=(1/lambda)ln(a/x0) and may not transfer to a multi-dimensional strange attractor with structured initial-condition geometry. The lambda-lock argument shows the strong (single deterministic strange-attractor, lambda_1>0 as the SOURCE of variability) form is unsupported on the flagship HVC example; it does not test hippocampal replay or cortical preparatory sequences, and direct local-Lyapunov estimates from neural trajectories remain absent.
